metadata.title: The Diner Break-In
metadata.description: A small-time overnight burglary hits a 24-hour diner after a back-door break-in, with cash missing and no injuries reported.
metadata.briefing: A 24-hour diner reports a forced back door and missing cash before dawn. You'll use the call log and a POS export to narrow down who was on the hook for access and timing.

assets.title: Back Door Forced-Entry Damage
assets.description: Crime-scene photo of the diner’s rear service door showing forced-entry damage and fresh tool marks. Captures the latch/strike area and surrounding frame to compare entry method against suspect access and familiarity with the door’s quirks.

assets.title: Register Closeout Paperwork on Office Desk
assets.description: Crime-scene photo of the office desk showing the overnight register closeout paperwork left in place after the break-in. Visible timestamps and handwritten totals help anchor the closeout timing relevant to staff movements around 03:18.

assets.title: Cash Drawer Condition After Theft
assets.description: Close-up evidence photo of the diner’s register cash drawer immediately after the reported break-in, showing the compartments and remaining contents. Used to document the loss condition and corroborate what was taken during the 03:18 entry window.

assets.title: 911 Call Reporting the Break-In
assets.description: Audio recording and transcript of the 911 call reporting the diner break-in. Captures the initial timeline, caller observations, and immediate actions taken by staff before officers arrived.

assets.title: Overnight Supervisor Incident Statement (Mara Kline)
assets.description: Written incident statement by overnight shift supervisor Mara Kline describing her actions, observations, and staff locations during the reported break-in window. Used to anchor the internal timeline against POS closeout and office landline activity.

assets.title: POS Transactions & Closeout Export (02:30–04:00)
assets.description: Point-of-sale export covering transactions and register closeout activity between 02:30 and 04:00 on 2026-05-11. Used to anchor register activity and the closeout window against staff movements during the reported 03:18 break-in.

assets.title: Office Landline Call Log (Night of Incident)
assets.description: Call-detail record extract from the diner's office landline covering the overnight shift on 2026-05-11. Used to corroborate the claimed vendor call and place staff in the office during the 03:18 break-in window.

assets.title: Nearby Store Camera Stills Facing Service Alley
assets.description: Three grainy overnight surveillance stills from a nearby convenience store camera aimed down the service alley behind the 24-hour diner. The frames capture the alley approach and back-door area around 03:18, showing limited sightlines and a key blind spot near the dumpster enclosure.

assets.title: Toolmark Comparison Report – Rear Service Door (Back Door Forced-Entry Damage)
assets.description: Forensic comparison of toolmarks on the diner’s rear service door latch/strike area. Findings indicate toolmark characteristics consistent with a flat prying tool and supportive of association with Dennis Yu, subject to stated limitations.

emails.from: Chief of Police, Eugene Police Department
emails.subject: Immediate Assignment: Overnight Break-In at 24-Hour Diner (Eugene) — Discreet Response Required
emails.body:
Detective Alex Morgan,

I’m assigning you the overnight burglary at the 24-hour diner in Eugene, Oregon. Entry appears to have been made through the rear service door at approximately 03:18 on 2026-05-11, with cash taken from the register/cash drawer and no injuries reported. Treat this as time-sensitive—our window to preserve scene integrity, recover usable impressions, and lock down digital records is closing.

The reporting party/victim is the diner’s overnight shift supervisor, Mara Kline. Ensure her incident statement is formally captured and that staff access, movements, and end-of-shift cash handling are documented without tipping internal personnel to the direction of the investigation.

Priority actions: secure and photograph the back-door forced-entry damage, confirm the condition of the cash drawer, and obtain copies of the POS transactions/closeout export (02:30–04:00) and the office landline call log for the same period. Request and preserve any available exterior camera coverage facing the service alley, including nearby business footage, before it is overwritten.

This matter requires discretion. Do not discuss working theories with diner staff beyond what is necessary to gather statements and evidence, and keep any suspect inquiries controlled and off-site where possible. Coordinate quietly with patrol for scene support if you need it, but avoid unnecessary visibility.

Provide me an initial assessment and recommended next steps as soon as you have verified the timeline and secured the digital and physical evidence streams.

emails.from: Chief R. Calder, Eugene Police Department <chief.calder@epd.gov>
emails.subject: Assignment: Overnight break-in at 24-hour diner (Eugene) — keep it discreet
emails.body:
Detective,

You’re assigned case_rookie_demo2, burglary at a 24-hour diner in Eugene. Reported forced entry at the rear service door around 03:18 on 2026-05-11 with cash missing from the register drawer. No injuries.

Priority is a clean timeline: staff locations, register closeout window, and the office landline call. Pull the on-scene photos (rear door damage, cash drawer, office paperwork) and the POS export/call log early. There’s mention of limited exterior coverage and an alley blind spot—verify what cameras do/don’t show.

Coordinate with the diner manager for access and preservation. Keep contacts low-profile; the business is concerned about reputation.

—Chief Calder

emails.subject: Incident details from overnight shift (05/11)
emails.body:
Officer/Detective,

Putting in writing what I told the responding unit. At about 03:15–03:20 I was in the office doing the register closeout. I placed a call from the office phone to our vendor line because we had a delivery issue (I don’t remember the person’s name).

I did not go to the back door during that time. Dennis (cook) had stepped out back earlier for a smoke break; he does that a lot. Tessa (server) had already clocked out and was waiting on a rideshare out front.

A few minutes later I noticed the register drawer was open/emptied and the back service door looked wrong (frame/latch area looked pried). I called 911 at 03:22.

I can meet today if you need me to walk through where everyone was standing.

—Mara Kline
Overnight Shift Supervisor

emails.subject: FWD: Dennis Yu message re: last night
emails.body:
Detective,

Forwarding a message Dennis sent me this morning after I asked all staff to document what they recall.

—Forwarded message—
From: Dennis Yu <dennis.yu@eugeneforkdiner.com>
Subject: Re: 5/11 overnight

I didn’t break in. I went out back for a smoke around 3-ish like I always do and came back in. I didn’t see anyone else out there. The back door sticks and sometimes you have to push it to latch—everyone knows that. I didn’t have any tools or anything.

—End forwarded message—

Let me know if you want scheduled interview times; I can have staff available this afternoon.

Janel Ortiz
General Manager

emails.subject: Lab Results: Toolmark Comparison – Rear Service Door (Case case_rookie_demo2)
emails.body:
Detectives,

We completed toolmark review of the submitted photo set for the diner’s rear service door forced-entry damage (asset.back_door_forced_entry). The latch/strike area shows deformation and contact marks consistent with insertion and levering by a flat, prying-type tool (e.g., screwdriver/small pry implement), with indicators of repeated insertion attempts.

Across the visible mark clusters, the class features and overall morphology are internally consistent and support the interpretation of a common tool type/edge condition contributing to the damage. Because the examination was photo-based only (no physical door hardware and no exemplar tool submitted), we cannot perform microscopic source-level comparisons or uniquely identify a specific tool.

Within the investigative context provided, the observed toolmark characteristics are assessed as supportive of association with Dennis Yu as a plausible user of a flat prying implement during the forced-entry event at approximately 2026-05-11 03:18. Please see the attached report for full methodology, limitations, and conclusion language.

suspects.name: Mara Kline
suspects.relationship: Shift supervisor at the diner; responsible for nightly register closeout
suspects.motive: Mara has been under pressure about cash shortages and could have reason to hide an over/short discrepancy after closing out the register. A burglary would conveniently explain missing cash without pointing to internal errors.
suspects.alibi: At the time of the break-in she was on the floor handling the register closeout and a vendor call from the office phone, then returned to the dining area. The office phone call and POS closeout timestamps place her inside and away from the back door during the window of entry.
suspects.background: Mara is a detail-oriented overnight lead known for keeping tight control over cash procedures and end-of-shift paperwork. She’s been covering extra nights due to staffing gaps, which has made her short-tempered but also more visible on cameras and in logs. Coworkers describe her as strict rather than sneaky, with a strong interest in keeping the diner’s numbers clean.

suspects.name: Dennis Yu
suspects.motive: Dennis was behind on rent and had been complaining about reduced hours and tips, making the overnight cash drawer an easy target. He also resented management after being warned about taking too many back-door smoke breaks.
suspects.alibi: He claims he was on a smoke break behind the diner around the time of the break-in and then went back to the line to prep, saying he never left the property. A nearby store camera shows him outside earlier, but the key minutes around 03:18 fall into a blind spot near the service alley.
suspects.background: Dennis has worked the overnight line for about a year and is known for slipping out the back door during slow periods. He’s familiar with the back-door latch quirks and has been seen jiggling it to get it to catch. Coworkers describe him as reliable on the grill but increasingly stressed about money over the past month.

suspects.name: Tessa Harper
suspects.relationship: Employee at the diner; worked the overnight shift
suspects.motive: As a new hire juggling bills, she had a tempting view of nightly cash totals and knew when the drawer was most full. She was also anxious about making mistakes on the POS and could benefit from missing cash being blamed on “bad counts.”
suspects.alibi: Around 03:05 she clocked out and ordered a rideshare from the front lot, leaving before the reported break-in window. Ride history and the driver’s dashcam place her pickup at 03:12 and drop-off at her apartment at 03:29.
suspects.background: Tessa is a recent community-college grad on her first week at the 24-hour diner, still learning the POS and end-of-shift receipt routine. Coworkers describe her as polite but visibly stressed during rushes and overly worried about being blamed for register discrepancies. She tends to keep to herself, and her phone shows frequent budgeting and gig-app activity consistent with financial pressure.

suspects.name: Roy Sandoval
suspects.relationship: Regular late-night customer at the diner
suspects.motive: Roy has been short on money and showed unusual interest in how the diner handles cash, which could suggest he was sizing up an easy score. He also knows the overnight rhythm well from frequent visits.
suspects.alibi: At the time of the break-in, Roy was on an active rideshare trip across town, picking up a passenger near downtown and dropping them off near River Road. The trip and timestamps are corroborated by app logs and the rider’s receipt.
suspects.background: Roy is a familiar face on late nights, often parking outside to eat and charge his phone between rides. Staff recall him asking pointed questions about when the cash drawer gets pulled and who closes the register, which made them uneasy. Despite the suspicious curiosity, he’s generally polite and has no known history of violence at the diner.

suspects.name: Ellen Brooks
suspects.relationship: Hired cleaning staff for the diner’s overnight operations
suspects.motive: She resents repeated late payments and a recent complaint about her work, giving her a financial and personal grievance. She also has routine access to the service entrance, making theft seem low-risk.
suspects.alibi: She was clocked into her primary contract at Cascade Medical Offices from 02:45 to 03:55, then drove straight to the diner and arrived a little after 04:10. The medical office timecard and interior hallway cameras confirm she was on-site during the 03:18 break-in.
suspects.background: Ellen has worked early-morning cleaning routes in Eugene for over a decade, juggling multiple contracts to cover bills after a divorce. She’s known as methodical and quiet, and she keeps a strict schedule to avoid missing client access windows. She carries diner keys only for the service entrance, issued through her cleaning company rather than the diner directly.

timeline.event: Server Tessa Harper clocks out and requests a rideshare from the front lot, departing before the reported break-in window.
Rideshare pickup confirms Tessa Harper leaves the diner property.
Back door is forced; entry occurs through the service entrance consistent with visible damage and tool marks.
Nearby store camera coverage shows activity outside earlier in the night, but the key minutes around 03:18 fall into a blind spot near the service alley.
Overnight supervisor Mara Kline is in the office handling register closeout and a vendor call, placing her away from the back door during the entry window.
Line cook Dennis Yu reports being outside on a smoke break behind the diner around the time of the break-in; his whereabouts during the key minutes are not corroborated due to exterior blind spot.
Cash drawer is discovered in an emptied condition consistent with a quick grab of overnight cash rather than theft of equipment or inventory.
A 911 call is placed reporting the break-in and missing cash; no injuries are reported.
Case is opened by the chief for investigation.

forensicOutcomes.conclusionText: Comparative examination of the rear service door latch/strike damage identified toolmark characteristics consistent with use of a flat, prying-type tool. The observed class and individual characteristics are consistent with the suspected tool type and are evaluated as supportive of association with suspect Dennis Yu, within the limitations of toolmark examination.

Latent fingerprint processing of the cash drawer photograph did not yield any usable ridge detail suitable for comparison. Observed impressions were largely smeared and overlapped, preventing identification or exclusion of any individual.

Digital timeline review of the diner office landline call-detail records for 2026-05-11 did not produce any inculpatory linkage to a specific individual. The call timing is generally consistent with the supervisor being engaged on the office phone during the reported entry window, but the record set is not sufficient on its own to definitively place or exclude any party.

Digital review of the nearby store camera stills confirms a coverage gap/blind spot at the service-alley/dumpster enclosure during the critical minutes around 03:18 on 2026-05-11. No reliable identification of the entrant or vehicle activity can be made from these images for the entry window.

questions.prompt: What method best matches how the diner was entered during the break-in?

options.label: Forced the rear service door using a flat prying tool on the latch/strike area
Unlocked the rear service entrance using an issued key without causing damage
Entered through the front door by blending with customers during a lull
Pried open a side window to reach the register area

questions.prompt: Where did the burglar enter the diner?

options.label: Through the rear service (back) door after forced entry
Through the front entrance during normal customer access
By breaking a side window near the dining area
Via a roof access hatch above the kitchen

questions.prompt: Which suspect is most strongly identified by toolmark evidence on the forced rear service door?
Which timeline entry best shows why Dennis Yu’s whereabouts at 03:18 aren’t corroborated?

options.label: Store camera coverage has a blind spot near the service alley/dumpster during the critical minutes around 03:18.
Mara Kline is in the office on a vendor call and register closeout at 03:18.
Tessa Harper’s rideshare pickup confirms she left the property at 03:12.
The cash drawer is discovered emptied at 03:19, consistent with a quick grab.

solution.explanation: The rear service door’s fresh pry damage (Back Door Forced-Entry Damage) was forensically tied to Dennis Yu: the Toolmark Comparison found characteristics consistent with a flat prying tool and supportive of association with him, and the nearby store camera stills show a critical blind spot at the service-alley/dumpster area right at 03:18—exactly where Dennis said he was taking a smoke break. Mara Kline is cleared because the office phone call log and register closeout paperwork place her in the office during the entry window; Tessa Harper is cleared by rideshare records showing she left before 03:18; Roy Sandoval is cleared by active rideshare trip logs across town; and Ellen Brooks is cleared by her primary job timecard and hallway cameras placing her at Cascade Medical Offices at 03:18.
